newsitem.title: INDIA: India PM's Russia trip hinges on Yeltsin's health.
newsitem.headline: India PM's Russia trip hinges on Yeltsin's health.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda tentatively plans to visit Russia next month but the trip depends on ailing President Boris Yeltsin's health, Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said on Saturday.
Gujral told Reuters that Deve Gowda and he hoped to travel to Moscow on February 9 or 10. It would be Deve Gowda's first trip to Russia since being named prime minister last June.

The Indian foreign minister, who spoke after addressing a meeting of representatives of member states of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN), said he had put off his trip to Russia which had been planned for January 27-31.
"It's been postponed slightly due to Yeltsin's health," Gujral said.
Yeltsin is recovering from double pneumonia, which struck him earlier this month just two weeks after he returned to the Kremlin after undergoing heart surgery.
A brief visit to the Kremlin on Wednesday, less than two full days after he left hospital, failed to dispel doubts over Yeltsin's health and his ability to rule.
Gujral said bilateral issues would dominate discussions in Moscow. "Bilaterally India and Russia have very close relationships, in economy and other perceptions," he said.
During the Cold War, the former Soviet Union and India nurtured close ties. Moscow was India's biggest arms supplier and an important trade partner.
After the demise of the Soviet Union, trade tapered off, choked by India's large unpaid debt. But both sides have sought to expand economic relations, and India remains an arms buyer.

Earlier this month, the U.S. Defense News journal said India had agreed to buy two Kilo-class diesel submarines from Russia. Indian officials said the deal had not yet been approved by Deve Gowda's cabinet.
In November, India signed a contract to buy up to 50 Russian Sukhoi SU-30 MK fighter jets worth more than $1 billion.

During a visit by Russian Deputy Prime Minister Oleg Davydov to New Delhi in October, both sides pledged to strengthen cooperation in the metallurgical and power sectors and boost trade. They also agreed to speed up measures to construct a 2,000-megawatt nuclear power project in southern India.
